title: Borders Then and Now
description: A schematic block diagram (not a map) that steps through 1857, 1858, 1947, 1948, 1971 and 1972 to show how East India Company territory and British India, the princely states and Ceylon became India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka. An event panel gives dates and sourced ranges for Partition and the 1971 war.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
History
Colonialism
Partition of 1947
Bangladesh Liberation War
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Explain how British India became India and Pakistan in 1947 and how East Pakistan became Bangladesh in 1971.
Describe how the princely states, including Hyderabad and Jammu and Kashmir, joined or were disputed after 1947.
Contrast Ceylon's peaceful independence in 1948 with the violence of Partition and the 1971 war.
prerequisites: Knowing the eight countries of South Asia (Chapter 1)
Knowing what the East India Company was (Chapter 3)
keyQuestions: How did one colonial territory become several countries?
Why did some princely states join quickly while Kashmir became disputed?
misconceptions: Britain ruled every part of South Asia directly.
Partition violence happened on only one side.
Pakistan was always one block of land.
